title: Choosing a Wife
author: The Ways of a Gentleman
summary: In this piece from The Ways of a Gentleman, the author argues that no decision shapes a man's life more than his choice of wife, and that the excitement and emotion of a new relationship are insufficient foundations for lifelong commitment. Six qualities are recommended above all others: character over beauty, shared faith and values, peace over drama, a woman who would be a good mother, someone who strengthens rather than competes with a man's purpose, and the discipline not to rush. The author insists that beauty fades while character — kindness, humility, patience, integrity — only becomes more valuable with time. Shared faith provides a common destination that makes disagreements navigable. The conclusion frames marriage not as finding a perfect person but as two imperfect people committed to helping each other grow, serve, and build a life that honors God.
points: No decision will shape the course of a man's life more than the woman he chooses to marry — making character, faith, and values far more important selection criteria than attraction or emotion.

Character — kindness, humility, patience, honesty, generosity, integrity — is what carries a marriage through financial hardship, sickness, raising children, and every challenge a couple will eventually face.
Shared faith and moral convictions provide a common foundation that makes disagreements easier to navigate because both partners are ultimately moving toward the same destination.
A wise wife encourages her husband to grow and pursue his purpose rather than competing with him; the best marriages make both people better and function as a true partnership.
Marriage isn't about one person completing another — it's about two imperfect people committed to helping each other grow, serving each other faithfully, and building a life together.
quotes: no decision will shape the course of a man's life more than the woman he chooses to marry.
The right wife has the power to make your life extraordinary. She becomes your closest companion, your confidant, your greatest encourager, and your trusted sounding board.
It is character that carries a marriage through financial hardship, disappointment, sickness, raising children, career changes, and the countless challenges that every couple eventually faces.
Few things create more unity within a marriage than shared beliefs. When a husband and wife share the same faith and moral convictions, they possess a common foundation to build their family on.
Home should be the place where a man finds peace. The world is going to give him enough grief on its own.
Your children will learn far more by watching their mother than from anything you tell them.
Marriage isn't about one person completing the other. It is about two people helping one another become everything they were created to be.
